note: Faithful rendering of Avalokitavrata's gloss on the two kinds of karma and the epithet Supreme Sage; only minor looseness in how the lemmata are framed.

errors.english: Therefore, why would a momentary functional thing exclusively produce [a result], or why would the consequence be stated that it does not exclusively produce?
errors.why: The Tibetan cites the opponent's consequence ('why does a momentary thing not produce alone, why is it not solitary?') as the subject of a sentence that goes on to say it is refuted; the English turns it into the author's own question and inverts it.

fix.find: Therefore, why would a momentary functional thing exclusively produce [a result], or why would the consequence be stated that it does not exclusively produce?
fix.replace: Therefore, the consequence that was stated, "Why does a momentary functional thing not produce alone? Why is it not solitary?" ...

note: Accurate through the argument on single-moment production; the closing sentence garbles the opponent's prasaṅga.

errors.english: If the transformation possesses a distinction, one observes it as either rough or otherwise. One might think:
errors.why: The milk example (a distinction in transformation is seen as curdled or not) is part of the opponent's thought introduced by སྙམ་དུ་སེམས་པ, not an assertion by the author.

errors.english: just as a distinction in the cause of existence
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་སྲིད་པ is 'as the case may be (yathāsambhavam)', i.e. 'in whatever cause there is', not 'the cause of existence'.

note: Sound on the argument against the body as the cause of consciousness; a couple of parsing slips.

errors.english: From the direction of the Chilikun Lake
errors.why: སྤྱི་བླུགས means a water jug or ewer (kuṇḍikā/kamaṇḍalu): the lake is named 'Ewer'. 'Chilikun' does not render anything in the Tibetan.

fix.find: From the direction of the Chilikun Lake
fix.replace: From the direction of the Ewer (Kuṇḍikā) Lake

errors.english: that result which falls upon the head of the milkman thrown by the hand of peace
errors.why: ཞོ་རྫིའུ is a small pot of curd, which is thrown by Śānti's/Peace's hand and lands on someone's head; it is not a milkman.

fix.find: that result which falls upon the head of the milkman thrown by the hand of peace
fix.replace: that result: the curd pot thrown by the hand of Śānti falling on [his] head

errors.english: through peace itself
errors.why: ཞི་བ here is most likely the proper name of a character (Śāntā/Śānti, the mother of Gopāla) and should not be translated as the abstract noun 'peace'.

note: These are lexical glosses on a Vinaya narrative; the place name and the curd-pot episode are misread, and the rest is literal but mostly serviceable.

errors.english: except for that which is clean and has not been trodden upon
errors.why: With the previous side, the exception is grass in which living creatures do not breed (སྲོག་ཆགས་དག་མི་སྐྱེ་བ); the English replaces this with 'clean and not trodden upon'.

errors.english: Having encouraged them, Udayin had them settle in a place.
errors.why: གནས་འཆའ་བ is to take niśraya (formal dependence): Udāyin had the new monks take dependence on himself, which is what makes them his ཉེ་གནས.

fix.find: Having encouraged them, Udayin had them settle in a place.
fix.replace: Having encouraged them, Udayin had them take dependence (niśraya) on himself.

note: Good rendering of the end of the bedding rule and the start of the eviction pāyattika; the niśraya term is missed.

errors.english: [note: The Conqueror, the Blessed One, spoke those words in order to instruct the monks: "This is the second leaf
errors.why: In the Sanskrit, 'thus spoke the Blessed One' closes the verse, and 'iti Kṣemendra…' is a separate colophon; the note puts the colophon into the Buddha's mouth.

errors.english: The Gem of a Man was born into this world of Bliss-Goers [note: the realm of the Buddhas]
errors.why: The verse says a jewel of a man, through whom the Sugata (or the good path) is manifested, is born in this world; it is not a 'realm of the Buddhas'.

errors.english: It remains within a stainless mind.
errors.why: The verse describes the city as inhabited by meritorious people with minds as stainless as the Ganges, like sacred fords; the English makes the city 'remain within a stainless mind'.

note: Kāvya verses from the Avadānakalpalatā are only loosely construed, and the colophon note is misleading.

errors.english: Therefore, one should show patience even toward those beings who strive to destroy you.
errors.why: དང་བ is faith or serene confidence (prasāda), which picks up 'lack of faith is hatred' above; it is not patience.

fix.find: one should show patience even toward those beings
fix.replace: one should have faith (prasāda) even toward those beings

errors.english: can it not grant a state equal to the Sugata
errors.why: This is a rhetorical question expecting 'no' (a king, even when pleased, cannot grant Buddhahood, in contrast to beings); 'can it not' reverses it.

fix.find: can it not grant a state equal to the Sugata
fix.replace: can he grant a state equal to the Sugata

errors.english: Now, you shall also explain
errors.why: This is the author announcing his next topic: 'I shall now explain the purification of the body.'

errors.english: In brief, the sins of the body are exhausted by purifying the afflictions.
errors.why: The verse names two components, the exhaustion of sin and the cleansing of afflictions; the English turns them into a cause-and-effect relation.

errors.english: Just as a river flows toward the ocean
errors.why: The entire side is in verse (ślokas and long-metre stanzas), and it is rendered as running prose with the verse boundaries lost.

note: The general sense of the verses on anger and guarding virtue comes through, but there is a key-term error, a reversed rhetorical question, and a wrong speaker.

span_why: The opening two sentences ('If one refutes this by falsely attributing… Because it arises immediately after effort') translate the previous side's last line.

errors.english: The error regarding the predicate itself
errors.why: The lemma is 'deviation with respect to the OTHER probandum' (permanence, the counterpart of impermanence); dropping གཞན loses the point that the gloss explains.

fix.find: The error regarding the predicate itself
fix.replace: Deviation with respect to the other probandum

errors.english: This is because impermanence is not established by the property of being produced immediately after effort [note: in all cases, since lightning is impermanent but not produced by human effort].
errors.why: The Tibetan says the reason does NOT deviate with respect to impermanence: only the inverted reason, used to prove permanence, deviates. The English says the reverse, and its note backs the wrong reading.

fix.find: This is because impermanence is not established by the property of being produced immediately after effort [note: in all cases, since lightning is impermanent but not produced by human effort].
fix.replace: But with respect to impermanence, the reason 'being produced immediately after effort' does not deviate.

note: The jāti (futile rejoinder) analysis is largely followed, but the arthāpattisama passage is inverted, and the translation reaches back into the previous side.

errors.english: because it is logical that the essence of one distinct entity is separate from another distinct entity
errors.why: The Tibetan says it is NOT reasonable for the nature of one entity to be [the nature of] another, distinct entity.

fix.find: because it is logical that the essence of one distinct entity is separate from another distinct entity
fix.replace: because it is not reasonable for the nature of one entity to be [the nature of] another, distinct entity

errors.english: It is incorrect for space [note: original: (nam mkha'); space or ether] to possess a nature
errors.why: Continuing from the previous side, the subject is the qualities (pervasiveness etc.): they cannot be space's nature. The text does not deny that space has a nature.

errors.english: Similarly, there are no distinctions among the collection of the six categories
errors.why: The sentence says: similarly, of expressions like 'the collection of the six categories' or 'a row of mansions', if there is no difference [between the collection and its members], one must say how '[the] six' applies. The English turns this into a claim that the categories lack distinctions.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: referring to number and collection]
errors.why: ལྡན་པ here is the Vaiśeṣika quality conjunction (saṃyoga): number and conjunction are both qualities, so they exist only in substances. 'Collection' is not a quality.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because those two [note: referring to number and collection]
fix.replace: number and conjunction are likewise impossible [for them], because those two [note: number (saṃkhyā) and conjunction (saṃyoga)]

note: Covers the anti-Vaiśeṣika argument about space and its nature, but the first sentence is inverted and the six-categories passage is misconstrued.

errors.english: If a preceptor or an abbot
errors.why: གནས here is the niśraya teacher (ācārya), the counterpart of the upādhyāya (མཁན་པོ), and not an abbot. The same mistake runs through the whole side ('the abbot').

fix.find: If a preceptor or an abbot
fix.replace: If the preceptor (upādhyāya) or the niśraya teacher (ācārya)

errors.english: it is said that they should be separated from what is harmful
errors.why: The student helps the teacher to receive (མནོད་པ) the penance and the like from the saṅgha and to be released from it quickly; 'harmful' misreads the edition variant གནོད.

fix.find: it is said that they should be separated from what is harmful
fix.replace: it is said: [help him] to receive [the penance] and be released from it

errors.english: should not stay with a preceptor and an abbot, or not stay.
errors.why: The rule names three things (the རྣམ་པ་གསུམ referred to next) that someone with fewer than ten years since ordination may not do: act as upādhyāya, act as niśraya teacher, or live without dependence.

fix.find: should not stay with a preceptor and an abbot, or not stay.
fix.replace: should not act as a preceptor, nor as a niśraya teacher, nor live without dependence.

errors.english: This means that the abbot does not only ask questions
errors.why: The text says the teacher does not need to ask [permission] but otherwise performs the same services; the English says he does more than ask questions.

errors.english: causing them to abandon unpleasant places
errors.why: This is the standard pentad item 'dispelling discontent (anabhirati)', a mental state of dissatisfaction with the holy life, not leaving unpleasant places.

note: The key Vinaya terms (upādhyāya/ācārya/niśraya, receiving penance, discontent) are systematically misread, so the rules come out garbled.
